title: Bind observation pagination cursors to an authorized snapshot
context: Subject reads expose at most 64 observations. Reading older observations requires pagination that detects changes between pages while preserving existing response limits and access checks. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Add opt-in, single-partition observation pages using a cursor containing an offset and a hash of the scope, subject, eligible authorized observations, and complete records. Recompute the hash on each page and reject mismatches with a conflict requiring a restart.
consequences: Default reads remain capped at 64 observations; explicit pages return total and next_cursor metadata.
Changes to snapshot membership or record contents force pagination to restart.
Grants are checked before pagination; cursors do not grant access, and paginated scope unions are refused.
Explicit page reads scan eligible observations to fingerprint the snapshot without retaining server-side pagination sessions.
A remaining cursor indicates incomplete coverage; observations still require currentness verification.
